load_basis: Facility nameplate hosting capacity (bitcoin-mining hosting). Operator reported the 180 MW Ellendale facility operating at full capacity as of May 31, 2026; the ND PSC order in PU-24-332 refers to 'the full 180 MW capacity' Applied can take under the first electric service agreement (PU-22-371). Contract/nameplate capacity, not metered average load; service is largely interruptible.
notes: Energizing announced March 7, 2023 (ground broken Sept 8, 2022). Served under MDU's High Density Contracted Demand Response Rate 45 electric service agreement (ND PSC PU-22-371), mostly interruptible. The eleven unnamed OSM building ways osm:way/1422191468 through osm:way/1422191477 sit about 500 m northwest of MDU's Ellendale substation and are treated here as this one campus; that assignment rests on location and building layout, not on a labelled source, and the lat/lon is the centroid of those ways. Polaris Forge 1 (the adjacent AI campus) is a separate row.

site_name: Applied Digital Polaris Forge 1 (Ellendale AI campus, leased to CoreWeave)
load_basis: Built critical IT capacity in service at end of 2025: Building 1 phase 1 (50 MW) ready for service Oct 27, 2025 and phase 2 (50 MW) Nov 24, 2025, after which 'Building 1 now operates at its full 100 MW critical IT load'. In service only for roughly the last two months of 2025, so the 2025 annual-average load is a small fraction of 100 MW.
notes: 400 MW critical IT is the contracted CoreWeave buildout; MDU's second electric service agreement (APLD-ELN-02 LLC, PU-23-322, amended in PU-24-332, order Feb 5, 2025) allows up to 350 MW, in addition to the 180 MW under the first agreement. MDU's 2023 application describes the site as adjacent to the first Ellendale facility near the Ellendale substation; lat/lon is the inventory's existing point for this campus, not independently re-derived. Later milestones for reference: 175 MW live at June 30, 2026 and 250 MW at Oct 2, 2026 (operator releases). Single-tenant AI campus owned by Applied Digital; classed here as hyperscale.

load_basis: Facility nameplate hosting capacity (bitcoin-mining hosting). Operator reported the 106 MW Jamestown facility operating at full capacity as of May 31, 2026; it was a 100 MW facility with 83 MW online in May 2022. Nameplate, not metered average load.
notes: Not in our inventory. Otter Tail Power serves it under an electric service agreement with Applied Blockchain filed with a service area agreement between Otter Tail and Northern Plains Electric Cooperative (ND PSC PU-21-364 / PU-21-366, Sept 2021); the carve-out covers 30 acres for 'initial 100 MW operations' with a 41.6 kV extension about 300 feet from Otter Tail's substation. Ground broken Sept 14, 2021; ribbon cutting May 5, 2022; operator later described it as 'energized in 2022'. Local reports in 2022 said it could scale to 200 MW; no source found that the expansion was built, so planned buildout is left null. Location: co-located with the Otter Tail 345/115 kV substation about 7 miles north of Jamestown on ND Highway 20 (KFGO, May 5, 2022: https://kfgo.com/2022/05/05/applied-blockchain-celebrates-finished-project-with-ribbon-cutting/); lat/lon is the centroid of the rows of buildings mapped in OpenStreetMap immediately south of that substation, an approximate placement.

load_basis: News description, not a metered or operator-published figure: InForum (Mar 3, 2024) called it 'a 200 megawatt facility which is expected to use 700 megawatts once buildout is complete' and said SPP had limited the electricity that can be supplied until northwest grid upgrades are done. No 2025-specific load figure was found; treat as uncertain.
notes: Cryptocurrency-mining / HPC hosting campus on a 77-acre site west of Williston (Trenton Township). Announced Jan 26, 2022 with phases of 240, 500 and 700 MW; the Governor's release says Mountrail-Williams Electric Cooperative supplies the power (a Basin Electric member, via Upper Missouri). Contract terms are not public, so the arrangement is left unknown. Start year: InForum said it 'went into operation last year' (2023); KFYR reported phase one complete by May 2023 and the Grand Forks Herald (June 2023) said it had been 'operating for some time', so late 2022 cannot be ruled out. A directory site lists about 240 MW of current draw; not used. Williams County ordered power cut to phase two in June 2023 over code violations and the co-op declined pending court review.

load_basis: Total power capacity of the campus as listed on the operator's site page (100 MW, 20 acres). Nameplate capacity, not metered or 2025-specific load.
notes: Not in our inventory. Address 5601 11th Ave S, Grand Forks, ND 58201 (operator page); lat/lon from the U.S. Census geocoder for that address. Nodak Electric (wholesale supplier Minnkota Power Cooperative) describes Core Scientific as the largest of three data processing centers that arrived in Grand Forks in 2021 and says it 'energized two other Grand Forks data mining projects in 2021 as well'; the article implies but does not state the exact month Core Scientific was energized (a directory lists November 2021, full capacity March 2022; not used). Contract type not stated. The two other Nodak-served data-mining sites are unnamed and unsized in the source and are not included here.

load_basis: Not in service in 2025: construction was to start as early as September 2025 (InForum, Oct 4, 2025) and full commercial operation is expected in early 2027 (North Dakota Monitor via InForum, Mar 23, 2026). No source found for a first-building in-service date.
notes: Included only so the existing OSM point is not counted as 2025 load. About 280 MW planned; Minnkota Power Cooperative supplies Cass County Electric Cooperative, which sells to the data center, and Minnkota will own the new substation and line. The operator's July 2026 results describe 200 MW of critical IT load under development here. lat/lon is the inventory's OSM node, not re-derived.
